newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says inflation will rise but capped.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says inflation will rise but capped.

text.p: Indonesian State Planning Minister Ginanjar Kartasasmita said on Monday the government will try to maintain 1997 inflation below 10 percent, despite the weakness of the rupiah against the dollar.

"It is difficult for us to say inflation will not be affected by current rupiah developments. We hope we can still control inflation. We hope inflation will be in single digits," Ginanjar told reporters.

"We have predicted inflation at around six percent this year but that is before the rupiah weakness. Because of current developments it is hard to get that level. That means inflation will be higher than our prediction."
Indonesia's consumer price index rose 0.66 percent in July, compared with a fall of 0.17 percent in June.
The country posted an inflation rate of 6.47 percent in calendar 1996, compared with 8.64 percent in 1995. the government has previously said inflation would be capped below six percent this year.
